tips.comment: Something of a Sedgefield regular, this mare bids for her first hurdles win at the scene of her bumper triumph. As was the case that day, the red-hot William Maggs comes on board and takes 5 lbs off in the process. I would like Chris Grant to be in better form than he is and for her to have a little more time since the last effort at Musselburgh, but this is a poor race and she should overcome those factors.

The simulation of this race by my model has Lillistar coming in first, ahead of Suitably Surprised in second and Vanilla Dancer in third. Lillistar is carrying significantly less weight than the others in this race, which should make the difference over 2m 3f. 65 days since the last race is slightly on the longer side but means the horse will be fresh. Good ground suits this horse and it might go quick.

Struck at the third time of asking over hurdles in a 16.8f juvenile at this track in November 2023 but gradually regressed for Nigel Hawke. Ignored in the betting but promising start for new yard when fourth in 16.9f handicap at Newcastle in February. Since had a breathing operation and cheekpieces on.

Hasn't shown much form this season but was third over course and distance last October. Is dropping down the weights and dropped in distance today, which may benefit. Chance to get first win of the season in a weak race.
Horse has been shaping well recently and has a nice racing weight today. Tasty each way price on this one in an open looking race today.
Resumed winning ways when winning a three-horse race at Newcastle, then a credible third last time out. This is my nap for today.

First run for new yard and the change of scenery could have a positive effect. One hurdle win and six places, and although he hasn't won over fences yet, he hasn't had that many attempts. Dropped another five pounds and now twenty pounds below the initial chase mark. Strong market support in a weak race looks positive.

Fairly useful maiden on the Flat and runner-up 4 times over hurdles for Paul Nicholls. Didn't shape badly on chase debut at Newcastle and, though he failed to build on that next time, he'll be a threat now upped in trip granted a clear round (early faller at Catterick on latest start).
Swingingonthesteel won in fine form last time out. He will appreciate the quick ground, and the trip won't be an issue. No others have any form to challenge.

Swingforthefence can go well for the Candlish yard. Swingforthefence has a first run today but is a relation of a listed winner. This horse is an interesting newcomer for a race that the ground will help.

Strikes as the type to do better now that he is trying three miles, especially in a weak race where he is top weight off a mark of 95. Has not looked a natural over fences in two starts so far, but he is bred to make a chaser, and the visual impression that he gives is that this distance is required.

Won an Irish point and made the frame 3 times over hurdles for Dan Skelton last term. Yet to trouble the judge following half-a-dozen appearances in this sphere and it's probably best to look elsewhere.
One Man Party has been well backed here in a weak race. An unexposed type, probably capable of much better off a light-looking weight.

Glance At Midnight can go well for the Martin yard. Glance At Midnight has run unplaced in two races but ran a very good race at Doncaster last time out. This is a race where this horse can do better again with that run to work on.
Well-bred newcomer from a yard with an excellent bumper record. By Doctor Dino he makes plenty of appeal on debut in a winnable race.

Top weight again for the 2nd year running. Now 1 lb lower than the mark he defied to win this event last term. He carried top weight and all before him when taking this race last season. Despite jumping slightly right throughout, he still had more than enough to fend off Traprain Law just for 2L, with recent Aintree winner Sans Bruit 6L further adrift in 3rd place. He's yet to trouble the judge in 4 runs this season. He's run well on occasion, just struggled off his lofty mark. He unseated rider LTO in a very competitive renewal of the Red Rum. He was still travelling well at the time, yet to play his hand. The yard must think he's sound enough to appear here just 9 days later. This looks to be plan B for them. If he's unscathed from his mishap LTO, then I think he can repel all challengers again this year.

In quality form and looks set up for this. Is quick enough for good-soft over 2m and looks the value play in the race currently. Will surely go off shorter than its current mark. Looks a great chance in this race.
Won this race two years ago off ten pounds higher. Usually runs well in springtime and now tried in first-time cheekpieces. Looks cracking value.
The pace of the race should assist, and Mullins will have this horse ready for the race. The right price would be around 3/1, and I think it's too big in this field here. 9/2 is a great price.

Handicapper has left his mark untouched, which is probably fair given his last run was rather due to poor luck rather than actual error. He was a strong candidate for the Ultima last time out. The choice of Derek Fox, he was hampered by a faller at the very first fence, which seemed to knock the stuffing out of him very early on, sending him to the rear. He could never recover from that, eventually pulling up. Stablemate Myretown went on to win that race in decisive fashion. This race looks less demanding anyway, so maybe a blessing his mark wasn't touched. He's won over course and distance too, which always helps around here, having won a class 3 handicap cosily enough back in January. Personally, I see this fella as a Scottish National type of horse. I think that will be the aim for him next term anyway. He gets a good chunk of weight from the favorite in here. I think he can win this on these terms.
Some good form over hurdles, but seems better still chasing with some good efforts and a few weak ones. Can bounce back here trying a longer trip.

I think the County Hurdle form will prove to be strong, and Ethical Diamond was giving weight to the top two. Carries top weight here but just 1 lb higher than Cheltenham, and I'd expect him to prove to be closer to a 150 horse than today's rating of 144. Penny took a while to drop and showed really good flat form on quick ground in the summer before breaking his maiden on heavy ground two starts back, winning by 10L. One of four bullets for Mullins but looks to be on a steep upwards curve who can help him edge closer to retaining his UK trainer's title.

Looks like a ready-made winner here, representing the in-form Ditcheat yard of Paul Nicholls and Harry Cobden, who have struck 10 times in their last 30 runs (excluding Friday's Ayr results). Paul won this race in 2023 with Rubaud, so he knows what it takes to produce the winner. The Mullins horse should mean the price stays above 3/1.

She fits most of the trends here. Ran at the festival last time out, which is a plus. Her last win came over 2M, which is also a plus. Fergal thinks the world of this mare. It's easy to see why. She's got very strong form to her name, despite running two lesser races the last twice. Her run in the Greatwood looks rock solid, running on similar ground to this. She ran a cracker to finish a 3L 3rd behind Burdett Road. She was sent off 85/40 favorite for that race. That tells you she's well thought of. The winner has franked the form since, finishing 2nd in the Champion Hurdle. She managed to rack up a 6-timer before that. She hammered this season's champion hurdle winner Golden Ace in her Grade 2 bumper win at Aintree. So clearly a classy horse. The ground is essential to her. She needs it faster, preferably. Mares don't do too badly in this race, with 3 of the 20 runners winning.

Ooh Betty is a talented mare when ridden prominently. She has disappointed when held up twice this season. Her run at Ascot this season was full of promise, and she carries a low weight in a very competitive heat.
Looks a fantastic each way bet, should be around 7/1. Loves it in Scotland. May lack a bit of class but can certainly handle itself in this type of race. Definitely worth a few quid.
Still unexposed and ahead of the handicap. Perfect suitability for the likely pace of the race. Still has stamina in abundance. Looks the most likely winner for this one.

Broke her maiden at Newcastle in February on her return from some time off. She has been given plenty of chance to recover from that and now steps up in trip on her handicap debut. Her dam is a full-sister to a Midlands National winner, so no shock if that generates a fair jolt of improvement.
Rockola Vogue has been very consistent and looks to have a nice handicap mark. She is by Jukebox Jury and out of a Presenting mare so should improve for the step up to three miles.

Fox's Fancy looks the way to go here in this class 2 handicap hurdle and is the value pick in the race at the time of writing in my point of view was last seen at this venue over the 2 mile 5 furlong trip where finishing a clear of rest 2nd/11 in a race won by Ruby Island who also runs here however Fox's Fancy holds every chance of reversing the form with that rival and going a place better this time out as she meets that rival on better terms this time out and they race over the 3 mile trip this time out and that is likely to benefit Fox's Fancy better his jumping is also much better than Ruby's Island's giving Fox's Fancy a clear advantage over a larger trip in a race that should be run to suit given the horses enrolled to run hear and with an ideal gallop at her disposal Miss Lucinda Russell's lightly raced mare can prove to be much better than a current operating mark of 113 over hurdles jockey P W Wadge takes the ride and can give Fox's Fancy the perfect ride here at Ayr must be considered

Steps right up in distance today. Running over 1M further than he's ever run over. His trainer knows the time of day. Surely he thinks this horse can stay the trip. The market tends to agree with that theory also. He's very lightly raced over fences. Just 3 runs to date, despite still being a maiden. He's run in much better races than this one. Stats tend to be against this fella. 5 of the last 6 winners of this race won LTO. Tbf, prior to that, only 2 of the previous 11 winners had won LTO, so that doesn't overly concern me. He won over hurdles at this meeting last season, just coming out on top in a battle to the line with Major Fortune. Tbf, he was giving 18lbs in weight to the runner-up. His penultimate chase run was fine. He finished a decent 3rd behind stablemate Champ Kiely. This fella is a former P2P winner and looks every inch a chaser. I'm hopeful this type of trip can unlock a vast amount of improvement.

This looks like the best bet for the Mullins team, and this is the only reason for the bet, to be honest. Looks like a plot as it's so lightly raced compared to his other runners. Will stay, in my opinion. Looks like a great bet.
This horse is an out-and-out stayer who won well last time out over 3 miles and 4 furlongs. Carries a featherweight and will be running on when many have cried enough.

Five runs this campaign, form 13132, progressing nicely. Beaten just 2L last time out in a useful-looking contest and should be fresh for a big run after a six-week break. Going conditions will be ideal, unexposed over this longer distance, still room for improvement from the 7yo. Strong jockey change, still on a handy low mark.

3/11 winning favorites, 4/11 top 3 in the betting. 10/11 carried 10st - 11st3. Won 2 on the bounce before 4th to Victtorino in the 3m Swinley handicap. Followed that up by running a decent race in 3rd when he fell at the last in the NH Cup at Cheltenham. That was 3m6f and could expect the extra distance to bring about even more improvement. Novice chasers have a strong record in this.

Mullins bingo in here, but I feel like Spanish Harlem was worth siding with being 4 lbs lower than when 4th in this last year. He’s had his mileage steadily increasing over 3 runs this season, which culminated in a decent effort in the National Trial, which has seen the front 3 do something for the form. He might need a bit of rain to be seen to bear effect, but if he can be ridden a bit more positively knowing he’ll get the trip, I’d hope Hayes, who was desperately unlucky in the National, can smuggle him into this late on.

Probably rather foolishly taking on the legend that is Willie Mullins and his entries. However, trainer Nicky Richards has previous and won this in 2019 with his 10-year-old Takingrisks, ridden by today's jockey Sean Quinlan on board Famous Bridge. The 9-year-old Fame And Glory gelding ticks a lot of the boxes. He has 7 wins and 5 places from 20 jump races, with 5 wins and 3 places coming from just 14 chase runs. He is a course winner and will love the ground and has won and placed in this grade. All in all, at 22/1, he's my e/w play.
Flash De Touzaine finished 4th in this very race two years ago. Won well last time out and can reward each way support in this race.
Was 4th in this race last year. Comes back a huge 10lb lower this year. Given a clear round, he should feature at the end.

Our Power has won each of his last 3 chases on good ground, and that looks to be the key here where many of his rivals would prefer some cut. The excellent 3lb claiming Conditional Dylan Johnston has been booked for the last 3 rides and been placed each time over inadequate trips. The horse was going well in the 2023 Grand National until stumbling badly 2 out and losing all chance, but that was a clear indication that he could well be suited by this extreme test of stamina.

With each-way playing down to 6th, I think it's worth chancing one with a featherweight. With a 7lb claimer on top, his mark is down to 119, which is only 1lb higher than when winning at Aintree in December 2023. He has run well in his 7 starts since, finishing placed on 4 occasions (runner-up 3 times), all off higher marks than today's. With little weight on his back (9st 11lb) and over a marathon trip, he could well run a place for a yard that will be trying desperately for prize money as they are chasing the trainers' title.

GROZNI looks a huge price here at 50/1. The selection ran a very respectable 6th in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham off a mark of 129. He's been dropped 2lb by the handicapper for this and has a 5lb claimer onboard. The step up in trip is an unknown but he was outpaced 4f out last time out over 3m 2f, so the extra 5f should help.

Been stung by this horse before when he refuses to run/compete. Talented horse on his day, has proven that he can stay the trip with a strong 2nd at Uttoxeter on 16/3/24 over 4m 2f at the Midlands Grand National. If (big if) he wants to run, he can get top 6. Different jockey this time, also claiming 3lb.

Two starts over hurdles for the 5yo. Runner-up on his debut during Feb. He was a narrow maiden hurdle winner four weeks ago but always in control, jumped well and sprinted through the line - capable runners in 2nd and 3rd. More to come from this one and has an attractive opening handicap mark.

Queensbury Boy looks underrated looking at the betting here. The Willie Mullins horse looks very short for what he has achieved. The selection is a strong traveller and being by Doyen, he will be suited by the dry ground.

Dysart Dolomite is a 5yr-old son of Walk in the Park ex Dysart Dancer thus a half brother to Dysart Dynamo by Westerner. This homebred makes his racecourse debut here in this bumper. He'll be ridden by Mr PW Mullins for his father WP Mullins. Stable is in top form at the moment & he makes the journey across the Irish Sea for this outing. He's one for your horse tracker.

Lightly raced 4yo, progressive last year. Two starts back he was beaten a nk in a Group 3 over this 12f trip - the winner won the Group 1 St Leger on his next start. He won a useful looking US £830k Grade 3 when last seen. Comes here after a 7 month break but he won on his return last spring and could be set for a big year - he does have an entry in the Group 1 Coronation Cup at Epsom in the summer. Loves the quick ground and should be a big player in this Group 3 contest.
Looks the best in the race, best engine for sure. Draw may hinder, but if not dealt with, looks to have the best chance by far in this race and could easily run off towards the end.

Only 2/11 winning favorites, 8/11 top 3 in the betting. 7/11 rated 105+ and only 2 had a run this season. More of a guessing game than I would usually play this early in the season. However, it is a G2 and G3 winner with placed G1 form when 1.25L 2nd to Lake Victoria in the Moyglare. Exactly 3rd and Bedtime Story 5th are both very useful horses, and the winner went on to win 2 more G1, including the Cheveley Park and Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf, when overcoming being hampered to win by 1.5L. Sangster is at a 23% strike rate currently, so fitness can be optimistic, and I simply think she's a good horse, more than capable of winning one of these. I wouldn't like to put anyone off the 40/1 available for the Guineas to run a place.
Mountain Breeze is from a top stable, and the stable jockey is on board. So, a big run from this horse is expected, and the ground trip is spot on.
Lope De Vega bred filly Better Times Ahead looked a very useful prospect when winning on her debut at Newmarket last November. This race will tell us more today.

Rashabar sets the standard the rest have to reach with his 5 starts as a juvenile, including winning the Group 2 Coventry before being touched off in a pair of Group 1s. The latest of which was having been stepped up to 7f. His yard won this two years ago with Isaac Shelby - also the class horse in the field - and conditions will be fine, having won at Royal Ascot on good to firm, but his two G1 2nds have had a bit more cut in the ground.
Will go off shorter than this, so take the price while you can. Made all last time and still unexposed.
Trained by Ed Walker, Noble Champion showed much improved form on his second run as a 2yo when winning at Lingfield Park in November. He could be very useful.

As discussed in the Metal Merchant tip, James McHenry has every chance here. He does well when fresh and is improving all the time. I've taken the selection to fill second place but if Metal Merchant has issues in running this horse will take the winners spot.

Looks the most likely winner in this, even though badly handicapped. May need to make up 8 lbs, but has the draw and has just recently run a blinder in Dubai, making this a great bet in this race. Should win.

Last year's winner beat the very good yardstick Godwinson in this race, and that was on good to soft, whereas his previous wins were on better ground. So he could be even better on seasonal debut this time around on the drying ground. He followed that up with an excellent 2nd to Sonny Liston again over this C&D, and it turned out that SL was well handicapped that day, so that was also a great effort. He's 1lb higher now than that 2nd place, and unlike many of these, we know he's capable of landing this one. The 5yo looks a decent bet to me at 11/2.

The 5yo had a light campaign last year but did post a couple of big RPR ratings in defeat. He ran well in the 16 runner Golden Mile £77K handicap last August, over this 8f trip on quick ground. He returns from his winter break on a handy looking mark, strong jockey booking and the yard is in good form.

Trained by Charlie Hills, this looks very much like an early season target race for Cogitate. Lightly raced for a 4-year-old, he was last seen at Kempton Park 143 days ago. He is a course winner here.

Solid juvenile and ran well on this card last year when a close fourth in the Greenham. Went backwards from there and has been gelded since he was last seen. This trip looks his best and fresh might not be a bad time to catch him.
This horse was a very talented 2-year-old before being mainly disappointing last season. Showed glimpses of form on his final outing last season, and if back in form, looks well handicapped.
A hold up horse so John Spencer has been booked to get him home in the last 100 yards. Has plenty of scope to improve at this distance. Paul Cole is no mug and he hasn't been sent here for a day out.

Parkland was sent off at just 9/4 in a hot Kempton maiden on his 2nd start to get the better of the odds-on favorite but had to settle for 2nd place where the winner was much the better. It does, however, raise an interesting point that he was clearly expected to give the winner a run for their money, and that winner is now a Group 1 winner no less (rated 122), which speaks volumes about this horse's potential ability. This is his first run on good ground on just his 6th start, which should suit on breeding (sire's progeny are also 2 from 5 over C&D), and this mark of 75 could well be a winnable one.

I can't resist a small win bet on this one, which is likely to put in an all-or-nothing type performance, I suspect. This joint bottom weight has been 2nd in both her attempts over C&D (off 66 and 50), and the 4yo races off just 46 here. The jockey is also somewhat of a specialist at this tricky course. He has one of his best strike rates at the course, and the horse is drawn well to get away with a quick break and attempt to hopefully bag a good position just in behind the leaders. Looks way overpriced on the evidence of those two C&D runs.

Didn't show much in three runs for a mark, but they all came in a five-week spell earlier in the year. Half-brother won on his handicap debut earlier in the week, and she may well be capable of doing the family double now that she enters this level. Yard has an excellent record when they send runners to this track.

Hostelry has immediately caught my attention here was last seen at Southwell 32 days ago where finishing 9th/12 however that was her return run after a 154 day break now returning to a suitable turf track with ideal ground conditions and is likely to be much fitter and a lot alert with that run on the all weather under her belt Mrs R Carr's mare is more than capable of bouncing back to form here currently operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 53 Hostelry looks poised to strike here and worth noting she is now operating a total of 10lb below her last winning mark in a race that should be run to suit given the horses enrolled to run here jockey Kaiya Fraser takes off a handy 3lb here which only enhances her good looking claims here price at the time of writing represents decent value and must be taken seriously and accordingly
